long_biography.plain_text:
Denmark is a constitutional monarchy in which the national government exercises executive authority through ministers. The prime minister leads the cabinet, while ministries prepare policy, administer legislation and oversee public responsibilities within their respective fields.

Central administration also includes agencies and other authorities responsible for regulation and public services. Cabinets and officeholders may change after elections or reshuffles, but the government continues as the executive machinery of the Danish state. The name denotes that enduring public institution rather than a particular prime minister, minister, civil servant or member of the royal family.
